issue_context.title: fstab generated Requires= dependency on mount is missing escaping
issue_context.body:
**systemd version the issue has been seen with**
systemd 247.3 (though it's present in latest main)

**Expected behaviour you didn't see**
 Example contents of /etc/fstab:
```
LABEL=/mnt/d0   /mnt/d0         rtxfs x-systemd.requires=/dev/disk/by-partlabel/\\x2fmnt\\x2fd0 0 2
```
On v246 this correctly generates Requires= dependencies for /mnt/d0 that looks like:
```
Requires="dev-disk-by\\x2dpartlabel-\\x5cx2fmnt\\x5cx2fd0.device"
```

**Unexpected behaviour you saw**
On v247 the example incorrectly generates:
```
Requires="dev-disk-by\\x2dpartlabel-x2fmntx2fd0.device"
```

I've bisected this to 0645b83a40d1c782f173c4d8440ab2fc82a75006. cc @keszybz in case you have a quick fix. I can look at it tomorrow since it's bedtime here.
comments:
Duh, I made a deep dive down into the parsing code, and it was mind numbing.
But it turns out that the bug report is buggy too: v246 does **not** behave like this:

```console
$ git describe
v246
$ cat fstab
LABEL=/mnt/d0   /mnt/d0         rtxfs x-systemd.requires=/dev/disk/by-partlabel/\\x2fmnt\\x2fd0 0 2
$ rm -rf /tmp/y && mkdir /tmp/y && SYSTEMD_FSTAB=fstab build/systemd-fstab-generator /tmp/{y,y,y}
$ grep Requires /tmp/y/mnt-d0.mount
Requires=dev-disk-by\x2dpartlabel-\x5cx2fmnt\x5cx2fd0.device
```

I'll file a PR to restore the same behaviour.
I'm not sure if we ever didn't do escaping. Right now getmntent() returns the unescaped string already.

Oh geez I'm so sorry the `Requires=` lines  I pasted were from `systemctl show -p Requires`. The actual file difference is as you described

v246 (good)
`Requires=dev-disk-by\x2dpartlabel-\x5cx2fmnt\x5cx2fd5.device`

v247+ (bad)
`Requires=dev-disk-by\x2dpartlabel-x2fmntx2fd5.device`

Oh, OK. I got so caught up in the tests that I didn't see that the bug is actually not fixed ;(

PTAL now.

review_comments: Hmm, indeed, this is interesting. If this is done, escaping of the separator cannot be done. I think *some* users of strv_split() expect it, while others not. It's something to investigate independently.
Depends on how the prior `strv_split` with `strv_split_extract` behaved before https://github.com/systemd/systemd/commit/0645b83a40d1c782f173c4d8440ab2fc82a75006 I suppose.
